# Review: C-401 Debutanizer, Section 5.1 Column Control

**Recommendation: Do not issue for configuration.** Two findings would put wrong behavior into the DCS:

- **R-01:** The stated TIC-405 response is backwards and would make the loop unstable.
- **R-02:** The tuning values conflict with the issued tuning sheet.

The section also has no requirement IDs, no fail positions, and no abnormal handling.

## Findings

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-01 | Para 2, TIC-405 | **Contradiction and unsafe response.** "Reverse acting" is correct for reboiler steam: when PV rises, output falls. The sentence then says rising temperature *increases* steam. That is positive feedback, so the reboiler would run away hot. A configurator could follow either statement. | State the response explicitly: "When TT-405 temperature increases, TIC-405 decreases the FIC-420 setpoint." Keep "reverse acting" only if the control philosophy defines that term. |
| R-02 | Para 5, tuning | **Number in prose, and it conflicts with the source.** The narrative says Kc = 0.8, Ti = 12 min. The issued tuning sheet says Kc = 1.2, Ti = 8 min. The narrative must not hold tuning values. This conflict shows why. | Delete the sentence. Reference the tuning sheet by document number and revision. Check that nobody has already configured TIC-405 from the narrative values. |
| R-03 | Para 6, TT-405 failure | **Not testable.** "Should" and "approximately" cannot pass or fail at FAT. Detection of a bad PV, alarming, and the effect on FIC-420 are all unstated. | Define bad-PV detection by reference to the instrument index or alarm database. Define the TIC-405 mode on bad PV, the FIC-420 mode and setpoint, the alarm, and the operator recovery steps. See the draft below. |
| R-04 | Para 7, FIC-420 manual | **Not testable, and the effect on the cascade is undefined.** "Upsets" is not defined, and "may" is permission, not a requirement. The text does not say what TIC-405 does when its secondary leaves cascade: initialization, windup protection, and bumpless return. | Write this as mode-shedding behavior. On loss of cascade, TIC-405 tracks the FIC-420 setpoint. On return to cascade, the transfer is bumpless. Delete "during upsets." |
| R-05 | Para 3, LIC-402 / FV-402 | **Tag inconsistency.** A level loop output would normally go to LV-402, or to a FIC setpoint by cascade. "FV-402" implies either a missing flow controller or a wrong tag. | Confirm against the P&ID and instrument index. If a bottoms flow loop exists, state the LIC-402 to FIC cascade. |
| R-06 | All loops | **Control action not stated** for FIC-410, LIC-411, FIC-412, LIC-402, and PIC-430. The action of the hot vapor bypass depends on the configuration and the valve fail action, so it must be explicit. | Give the PV direction to output direction for each loop, as in R-01. |
| R-07 | All valves | **No fail positions** for FV-410, FV-412, FV-420, FV/LV-402, or PV-430. | Reference the instrument index for fail action. State the required DCS output on loss of the controller or I/O. |
| R-08 | Section | **Missing abnormal handling:** bad PV for every loop (not only TT-405), comms loss, and power loss with restart. The restart mode and output for each loop are not given. | Add an abnormal-handling table: loop, bad PV response, comms-loss response, restart mode. |
| R-09 | Section | **No requirement IDs.** Nothing can be traced to a FAT step. | Assign FR-C401-NNN to each requirement, with a test method. |
| R-10 | Para 1, FIC-412 | Operator-set distillate with reflux on drum level is a valid scheme. The narrative does not say whether FIC-412 has a cascade mode, setpoint limits, or a low-level response. If LIC-411 drives reflux to its minimum and the drum is still falling, nothing happens. | State the FIC-412 modes. Reference the setpoint list for limits. Say whether any override applies. |
| R-11 | Para 2, "Tray 5" | The tray numbering direction (top-down or bottom-up) is not stated. | Reference the column datasheet numbering, or state "tray 5 from the top." |
| R-12 | Section | No reference to states (start-up, total reflux, normal, shutdown), the cause-and-effect chart, the alarm database, or the SIS SRS for column overpressure. | Add cross-references. Confirm that overpressure protection is in the SRS and the relief study, not in this section. |
| R-13 | Section | Inconsistent terms: "controls," "sets," "manipulates," and "cascades" are used for different relationships. | Use one term per relationship: "TIC-405 output sets the FIC-420 setpoint (cascade)" and "LIC-402 output positions LV-402." |
| R-14 | Section | No open items list. R-01, R-03, R-05, and R-07 need decisions from process and operations. | Add an open items table with an owner and date for each. |

## Suggested rewrite (partial; resolve open items before issue)

**5.1 Column Control**

Tuning values are in the tuning sheet [doc no., rev]. Limits are in the C-401 setpoint list [doc no., rev].

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C401-001 | LIC-411 output sets the FIC-410 setpoint (cascade). When the LIC-411 level increases, LIC-411 increases the FIC-410 setpoint. | FAT: simulate a level increase and confirm the FIC-410 SP increases. |
| FR-C401-002 | FIC-412 operates in AUTO with an operator setpoint, within the limits in the setpoint list. | FAT: enter an SP outside the limits and confirm it is rejected. |
| FR-C401-003 | TIC-405 output sets the FIC-420 setpoint (cascade). When the TT-405 temperature increases, TIC-405 decreases the FIC-420 setpoint. | FAT: simulate a TT-405 increase and confirm the FIC-420 SP decreases. |
| FR-C401-004 | When FIC-420 is not in CASCADE, TIC-405 output tracks the FIC-420 setpoint. | FAT: put FIC-420 in MAN and confirm TIC-405 OP equals the FIC-420 SP. |
| FR-C401-005 | When FIC-420 returns to CASCADE, the transfer is bumpless. | FAT: return to CAS and confirm no step change in the FIC-420 SP. |
| FR-C401-006 | When TT-405 is BAD, TIC-405 goes to MAN and holds the last good output. FIC-420 holds its last setpoint in CASCADE. The DCS initiates alarm [tag] per the alarm database. | FAT: force TT-405 BAD and confirm the TIC-405 mode, the OP, and the alarm. |
| FR-C401-007 | When the LIC-402 level increases, LIC-402 increases the LV-402 [confirm tag, R-05] opening. | FAT: simulate the level and confirm the output direction. |
| FR-C401-008 | PIC-430 positions PV-430. When the column pressure increases, PIC-430 [opens/closes, open item OI-02] PV-430. | FAT: simulate the pressure and confirm the output direction. |

**Open items**

| OI | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-01 | Confirm the TIC-405 bad-PV response in FR-C401-006 with operations. | Operations lead | [assign] |
| OI-02 | Confirm the PIC-430 action against the hot vapor bypass configuration and the PV-430 fail action. | Process engineer | [assign] |
| OI-03 | Resolve the FV-402 vs. LV-402 tag and whether a bottoms flow loop exists. | Controls lead | [assign] |
| OI-04 | Add the abnormal-handling table (bad PV, comms loss, restart) for all loops. | Controls lead | [assign] |
| OI-05 | Confirm that no configuration used the narrative tuning (Kc 0.8 / Ti 12). | Integrator | [assign] |

I left the owners and dates blank because the excerpt does not name the project team. Operations must sign off FR-C401-004 to -006 before issue, because those requirements define what the operator sees during a cascade break.
